# API rate limits

The API rate limit is 60 requests per minute for Startup, 300 for Pro, and 1000 for Business, measured per workspace.
If you exceed the rate limit, the API returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header specifying how many seconds to wait before retrying.
Requests rejected with HTTP 429 do not count toward the daily request quota.
When the daily quota is exhausted, requests return HTTP 429 until the quota resets at midnight UTC.

# Authentication

The ForgeNest API authentication methods support API keys and OAuth 2.0.
Use API keys for server integrations and OAuth 2.0 for delegated user access.
Send an API key in the Authorization header as a Bearer token.
OAuth access tokens expire after 60 minutes; refresh tokens expire after 30 days.
Keep credentials secret and rotate a compromised API key immediately.

# Data retention and deletion

You cannot delete customer data immediately on request: deletion from active systems takes up to 7 days after approval, and backup copies expire within 30 days.
To request deletion of customer data, a workspace administrator must open Settings > Privacy > Delete data and submit the customer identifier.
The deletion request is reviewed within 2 business days; the administrator receives confirmation when active-system deletion completes.

Customer activity records are retained for 90 days unless an approved deletion request removes them sooner. Workspace administrators can export these records before requesting deletion.

# Pricing

ForgeNest offers a free Startup plan for startups at $0 per month, including 1000 API requests per day and 1 project.
The Pro plan costs $49 per month, including 10000 API requests per day and 10 projects.
The Business plan costs $199 per month, including 100000 API requests per day and 50 projects.
Each plan includes API access and webhooks. These fictional prices are in USD.

# Webhooks

Webhook delivery logs are retained for 30 days and can be viewed in the dashboard.
Each delivery log includes the event identifier, attempt timestamp, HTTP status, and response duration.
Failed webhook deliveries are retried up to 5 times over 24 hours.
Endpoints must return an HTTP 200 response within 10 seconds.
Verify webhook signatures with the signing secret shown in the dashboard.
